# sifty

> Free zero-shot text and image classification API. Send text and 2-26 labels you choose; get back the most likely label, or a probability for every label. No training, no account, no API key.

Qwen3.5-4B scores each label from next-token probabilities in one forward pass; it never generates text. Free tier: 1,000 units per IP per UTC day (a batch counts each text, a System One call each question), plus a shared daily cap. Over the limit answers 429 with Retry-After. One GPU is always on, so answers usually take about a second; during a traffic spike an extra GPU can take up to a minute to start. Requests pass through Cloudflare and RunPod. Request text, labels, results, and country/client metadata are retained in private logs for 3 days for usage analysis and debugging. Public statistics contain only aggregates. Do not send sensitive data.

## API

- `GET https://sifty.dev/<label>,<label>/<text>`: the label as plain text. `+` is a space; percent-encode `,` `+` `/` inside labels. Example: `https://sifty.dev/spam,not+spam/Win+a+free+iPhone` returns `spam`.
- `GET https://sifty.dev/?labels=<a,b>&text=<text>`: the same, as query parameters.
- Add `?verbose=1` to either GET for JSON: `{model, results: [{label, confidence, scores, ms}], usage}`.
- `POST https://sifty.dev/` with `{"input": "text" or ["up to 32 texts"], "labels": ["a", "b"]}`: one result per text.
- Images: add `"image": "<https URL or data:image/...;base64,...>"` to `POST /` (then `input` is optional text about the image), `/v1/score` (beside or instead of `context`), or `/v1/systemone` (asked about by every question); or `GET https://sifty.dev/?labels=cat,dog&image=<url-encoded URL>`. Uploads up to about 6 MB. Images are never stored.
- `POST https://sifty.dev/v1/score`: full request `{context, question, options: [{id, text}]}` and response with per-option probabilities.
- `POST https://sifty.dev/v1/systemone`: the TypeSafe System One protocol; the `typesafe-sdk` Python client works with `base_url="https://sifty.dev"` and `api_key="free"`, so code written for Jev only needs a different base URL. Noul, Choice and Score questions are supported. Probabilities come from an open model not trained for calibration. sifty is independent and not affiliated with TypeSafe AI.
